recording_rule: A record states one definition, theorem, conjecture, heuristic, nonclaim, or source defect with exact hypotheses and locators. Distinct presentations remain distinct until an explicit interface is proved. A survey statement is not silently upgraded to its cited primary theorem.

name: Additive even-test/Fourier presentation of the zeta explicit formula

objects.test_function: h on the strip |Im r| <= 1/2 + delta

hypotheses: h is analytic on |Im r| <= 1/2 + delta
formula_as_presented: sum over nontrivial zeros of h(s_n) = (1/(2*pi))*integral_R h(r)*(Gamma'/Gamma)(1/4+i*r/2) dr - 2*sum_p(log p)*sum_{n>=1}p^(-n/2)g(n log p) + h(i/2)+h(-i/2)-g(0)log pi
typing_issue: The source defines h in an r-variable but prints h(s_n) with s_n called a zero; the ordinate/shift convention is not typed in the displayed formula. No silent correction has been made.
nonclaims: This record does not identify this presentation with the multiplicative Mellin/local-place presentation.
This record does not license the later delta-test physical trace formula, which the same source explicitly obtains by ignoring convergence questions at lines 143-154.

name: Sharp Chebyshev and truncated zero-sum presentations
hypotheses: psi_0(x) is the average of the two one-sided values
the zero sum is conditionally ordered by grouping rho with its conjugate
the displayed error estimate for psi(x) uses a truncation height T

formula_as_presented.rh_consequence: assuming all rho=1/2+i*gamma and taking T=x gives psi(x)=x+O(x^(1/2)(log x)^2)

nonclaims: The truncated formula is not the same data type as a test-function distributional formula.
The source states, but this record does not independently reprove, the converse equivalence of the displayed square-root error estimate with the zero-location condition.

name: Multiplicative Mellin and rational-place presentation
hypotheses: f is continuous and piecewise C1 with first-kind jumps averaged at exceptional points
for some delta>0, f(x)=O(x^delta) as x->0+
convergence_note: The zero sum is stated to be generally conditionally convergent.
nonclaims: The source attributes the general formula to Guinand and Weil; primary-source hypotheses and convergence conventions remain to be checked.
No equivalence with LITSTMT-20260824-0001 or LITSTMT-20260824-0002 is asserted here.

name: Montgomery Poisson-weighted explicit formula
hypotheses: printed proposition assumes the zero-location condition and writes rho=1/2+i*gamma with gamma real
lines 207-211 give a distinct unconditional reparameterization rho=1/2+i*gamma with gamma complex
proof_route: Landau's partial logarithmic-derivative formula is evaluated at s=3/2+i*t and s=-1/2+i*t, then the two identities are subtracted and the functional equation controls zeta'/zeta.
nonclaims: The unconditional complex-gamma convention is not interchangeable with the real-ordinate convention in estimates without rechecking every absolute-value step.
This weighted identity is not the full pair-correlation law.

name: Montgomery weighted pair form
hypotheses: the displayed zero-ordinate form uses real gamma
nonclaims: The symbol F(alpha) in the source retains T-dependence.
The x=T^alpha substitution is recorded, not used to erase the x- and alpha-presentations.

name: Montgomery alpha-range theorem as presented by Goldston

citation_identity.title: The pair correlation of zeros of the zeta function
citation_identity.container: Analytic Number Theory, Proceedings of Symposia in Pure Mathematics 24

conclusion: F(alpha,T) is real, even, and nonnegative; uniformly for 0<=alpha<=1-epsilon, F(alpha,T)=alpha+o(1)+(1+o(1))*T^(-2*alpha)*log T.
extension: Goldston records that a sieve bound improving O(x log x) to O(x) extends the range through 0<=alpha<=1.
proof_dependencies: Montgomery-Vaughan mean value theorem for Dirichlet polynomials
sieve bound for the endpoint extension
nonclaims: No statement for fixed alpha>1 is proved here.
This theorem does not state the full sine-kernel pair-density formula.

name: Support-limited evaluation of pair-difference test sums
hypotheses: r and r_hat belong to L1
r_hat is supported in [-1,1] for use of the proved alpha range
Fourier convention r_hat(alpha)=integral_R r(u)exp(2*pi*i*alpha*u)du and r(u)=integral_R r_hat(alpha)exp(-2*pi*i*u*alpha)dalpha
the zero-location condition for the theorem input
consequence: Using the Fejer transform pair with 0<lambda<=1 yields the weighted asymptotic (1/lambda+lambda/3)*(T/(2*pi))*log T and hence the stated lower bound that at least (2/3-o(1))N(T) zeros are simple.
nonclaims: Compact Fourier support is a real theorem boundary, not a cosmetic technicality.
The consequence does not determine arbitrary interval indicators or the full pair measure.

name: Strong Pair Correlation Conjecture
statement: F(alpha,T)=1+o(1) uniformly on the stated bounded alpha range.
heuristic_dependencies: a Hardy-Littlewood prime-pair conjecture with a strong error term motivates the range 1<=alpha<=2-epsilon
the source explicitly distinguishes SPC from PCC
nonclaims: SPC is not Montgomery's proved alpha-range theorem.
SPC is not itself an interval pair-counting statement.

name: Pair Correlation Conjecture in interval-counting form
hypotheses: ordinates are counted with 0<gamma,gamma'<=T and 0<gamma'-gamma<=2*pi*beta/log T
statement: N(T,beta) ~ integral_0^beta [1-(sin(pi*u)/(pi*u))^2] du after division by (T/(2*pi))*log T.
related_theorem: Goldston states and proves that, assuming the zero-location condition, SPC implies PCC and the average-multiplicity simple-zeros conjecture.
nonclaims: The sine-kernel density is not proved by LITSTMT-20260824-0006.
PCC and SPC are logically distinct statements even though terminology in the literature sometimes conflates them.

name: Bulk GUE sine-kernel point process
statement: R_n(E_1,...,E_n)=det[K(E_i,E_j)] with K(E_i,E_j)=sin(pi(E_i-E_j))/(pi(E_i-E_j)); hence R_2(epsilon)=1-(sin(pi*epsilon)/(pi*epsilon))^2.
symmetry_classification_as_presented: integer-spin chaotic systems without time-reversal invariance -> GUE
integer-spin chaotic systems with time-reversal invariance -> GOE
half-integer spin with time-reversal invariance -> GSE
nonclaims: This is an ensemble limit theorem/presentation, not a theorem that zeta zeros are an operator spectrum.
GUE is not CUE; their matching local limits do not identify the finite ensembles.

name: Bogomolny-Keating finite-height two-point formula
hypotheses_and_unproved_inputs: Hardy-Littlewood prime-pair conjecture for the mean of Lambda(n)Lambda(n+r)
replacement of a sum by an integral

formula_structure.unfolded_limit: after height-dependent scaling, the diagonal and oscillatory pieces tend to the GUE two-point expression

source_self_classification: The source calls the derivation physical/heuristic, says the optimistic error is only supposed, and concludes that the random-matrix results discussed are not rigorously proved.
nonclaims: The label exact_R is an equation label, not a proof of exactness.
Numerical agreement does not change the theorem status.

name: Zeta-zero/GUE local-statistics correspondence
statement: After local unfolding at large height, the zero pair and higher local correlation statistics are conjectured to approach the corresponding GUE bulk statistics.
evidence_layers: Odlyzko numerical comparisons as reported by the surveys
missing_arrows: no fixed self-adjoint operator is constructed by these statistical statements
no map from individual zeros to individual random-matrix eigenvalues is supplied
no finite-height equality of point processes is supplied

name: Schumayer-Hutchinson collapse of theorem and conjecture
printed_claim: The source says Montgomery showed the full sine-kernel pair-correlation function under the zero-location condition.
conflict: Goldston's detailed account records only the weighted alpha-range theorem as proved and separately labels the full interval sine-kernel law PCC.
required_correction: Present the full sine-kernel law as conjectural; state the proved alpha/support range separately.
nonclaim: This record does not attribute the correction to a later author until Montgomery's original paper is content-read.

name: CUE characteristic-polynomial moments versus zeta moments
finite_ensemble_statement: For Haar U(N), the displayed characteristic-polynomial moment is product_{j=1}^N Gamma(j)Gamma(2*lambda+j)/Gamma(j+lambda)^2, with large-N factor N^(lambda^2)G(1+lambda)^2/G(1+2*lambda).
zeta_conjecture: The corresponding zeta moment is conjectured to have arithmetic factor a(lambda), logarithmic growth (log T)^(lambda^2), and the same Barnes-G factor.

typed_difference.candidate_scale: N is compared asymptotically with log T

source_defects: The source labels the U(N) Barnes-G factor f_COE although the finite ensemble just computed is unitary/CUE.
The list of first values repeats f(1) where the 1/12 value belongs to lambda=2.
The historical name Ingram should be checked against the primary moment literature.
nonclaims: The finite U(N) integral does not prove the zeta moment conjecture.
N=log T is a model identification, not an invertible map of underlying objects.

name: Exact finite-N CUE absolute characteristic-polynomial moment

objects.matrix: U in U(N) with normalized Haar measure

proof_route: Write Z as a product over eigenphases, insert the CUE joint eigenphase density, transform the resulting N-fold integral to Selberg's integral, and evaluate it exactly.
continuation_boundary: The gamma product has meromorphic continuation in s. This continuation is not the Haar expectation outside the integrability half-plane without a separate regularized interpretation.
nonclaims: No zeta-function moment follows from this finite-dimensional theorem.
The theorem does not identify CUE with GUE as finite ensembles.

name: Exact finite-N CUE phase-ratio moment

objects.branch: arg Z is defined by the paper's continuous theta-i*epsilon prescription away from eigenphases

initial_integral_domain: the Selberg-integral derivation is initially justified by the inequalities translated at lines 420-425; the paper then analytically continues
nonclaims: Dropping the branch prescription changes the object.
Analytic continuation does not erase the initial integral-domain conditions.

name: Barnes-G coefficient for CUE absolute moments
hypotheses: Re(lambda)>-1/2 for the underlying absolute moment before meromorphic continuation
integer_specialization: For integer k>=1, the coefficient is product_{j=0}^{k-1} j!/(j+k)!; in particular 1, 1/12, 42/9!, and 24024/16! for k=1,2,3,4.
continuation_boundary: The Barnes-G quotient continues meromorphically beyond the initial moment domain; that continuation is a coefficient function, not automatically a convergent moment limit there.
nonclaim: This coefficient is the CUE factor only; it contains no arithmetic prime factor.

name: Joint CUE central limit theorem for log characteristic polynomials
hypotheses: theta is real and the logarithm branch is the paper's stated branch
conclusion: Re log Z(U;theta)/sqrt((1/2)log N) and Im log Z(U;theta)/sqrt((1/2)log N) converge jointly to independent standard normal variables.
coordinate_data: odd cumulants of Im log Z vanish identically
all higher normalized pure and mixed cumulants vanish in the limit
proof_route: Differentiate the exact generating products, express cumulants by polygamma sums, derive their large-N asymptotics, and use the exact joint generating product to control mixed cumulants.
nonclaims: Agreement with Selberg's zeta-value theorem after a scale choice is not a proof of Selberg's theorem.
Finite-N real and imaginary parts are not asserted independent.

name: Keating-Snaith mean-spacing parameter match
statement: Equating CUE mean eigenphase spacing 2*pi/N with the asymptotic zeta-zero spacing 2*pi/log(T/(2*pi)) gives N=log(T/(2*pi)).
nonclaims: A positive real effective dimension is not automatically an integer matrix size.
The parameter map supplies no map from individual zeros to eigenphases and no equality of finite point processes.
The paper's finite-height comparisons are model tests, not theorem transfers.

name: Keating-Snaith arithmetic Euler-product factor
definition: a(lambda)=product_p (1-p^(-1))^(lambda^2) * sum_{m>=0} [Gamma(lambda+m)/(Gamma(lambda)m!)]^2 p^(-m), interpreted by analytic continuation at removable parameter values where needed.
equivalent_coefficient: Gamma(lambda+m)/(Gamma(lambda)m!)=(lambda)_m/m! whenever the gamma quotient is defined.
role: This is the arithmetic prime factor in the conjectural leading coefficient for zeta absolute moments.
nonclaims: The finite CUE integral does not contain a(lambda).
The paper's truncated-Euler-product independence argument is heuristic, not a proof of the Euler product's role.
No maximal convergence domain is asserted by this record.

name: Keating-Snaith zeta absolute-moment conjecture
hypotheses_as_stated: lambda lies where the moment and limiting expression are defined
statement: (1/T) integral_0^T |zeta(1/2+i*t)|^(2*lambda) dt is asymptotic to a(lambda) * [G(1+lambda)^2/G(1+2*lambda)] * (log T)^(lambda^2).
historical_evidence_in_source: the lambda=1 and lambda=2 leading coefficients were known
then-conjectural lambda=3 and lambda=4 coefficients agree with the CUE Barnes-G values
finite-height Odlyzko data agree more closely after the arithmetic factor is included
nonclaims: The conjecture is not proved by the Selberg integral or by numerical agreement.
The paper does not establish a zeta-to-matrix object morphism.
This historical statement record does not claim to summarize all moment theorems proved after 2000.

name: Short-range CUE factor times long-range prime factor
heuristic: Finite-height zeta statistics split into a local random-matrix contribution and a long-range arithmetic contribution expressible through primes; exponentiating log-zeta heuristics suggests multiplying the CUE moment by a(lambda).
unproved_steps: truncate the Euler product at p<T/(2*pi)
transport the continuous effective dimension N=log(T/(2*pi)) to a finite matrix model
pass from log-statistic corrections to absolute moments
nonclaims: The words split and product describe the proposed leading model, not a proved factorization of random variables or measures.
Prime information is not negligible at finite height merely because the CUE local limit is accurate.

name: Primary refinement of the survey-level CUE moment record
corrections_and_sharpenings: the exact parameter match is N=log(T/(2*pi)), not merely N asymptotic to log T
the finite moment's initial domain is Re(s)>-1, equivalently Re(lambda)>-1/2 under s=2lambda
the computed ensemble is CUE/Haar U(N), confirming that the COE label in the survey is a typo
the value 1/12 is f_CUE(2), confirming the survey's repeated f(1) label is a typo
the primary bibliography names A. E. Ingham, resolving the survey spelling defect
nonclaim: This refinement does not retract the correctly typed theorem/conjecture separation already preserved in LITSTMT-20260824-0014.

name: Exact circular-beta characteristic-polynomial moment for COE, CUE, and CSE
hypotheses: beta is 1, 2, or 4 for COE, CUE, or CSE respectively
compatibility: At beta=2 and index k=j+1 this is exactly LITSTMT-20260824-0015.
nonclaims: No particular zeta or L-function family is assigned to beta=1 or beta=4 by this finite-ensemble theorem.
The later family-symmetry correspondence remains a separate conjectural interface.

name: Montgomery's normalized weighted pair form
hypotheses_and_objects: RH is assumed throughout the paper, so every nontrivial zero is written rho=1/2+i*gamma with gamma real
zeros in both sums are counted with multiplicity
exact_symmetries: Interchanging gamma and gamma' proves F_M(alpha,T) is real and F_M(alpha,T)=F_M(-alpha,T).
typed_relations: Goldston's x-presentation uses the bijection x=T^alpha for fixed T>1 and is not substituted away
the paper's pair-difference coordinate (gamma-gamma')log(T)/(2*pi) is related to, but not equal at finite T to, the local-density coordinate using log(T/(2*pi)); see MORPH-20260824-0009
nonclaims: The symbol F_M retains its T-dependence.
This definition does not itself state a limiting pair density or construct a spectral operator.

name: Montgomery's published alpha-range theorem
hypotheses: epsilon>0 is fixed for the uniform range and lower bound
conclusions: there is T_0(epsilon) such that F_M(alpha,T)>=-epsilon for all real alpha whenever T>T_0(epsilon)
the displayed asymptotic is uniform for 0<=alpha<=1-epsilon
published_endpoint_note: The paper says that with more effort the asymptotic could be shown uniformly throughout 0<=alpha<=1, but the printed proof establishes the stated 1-epsilon range. Goldston later supplies exact nonnegativity and records a sieve refinement through alpha=1; those later refinements are not retrojected into this theorem.
proof_dependencies: the zero-side squared mean over t
Montgomery-Vaughan's quantitative Parseval identity for Dirichlet series
the prime number theorem with error term
Cauchy-Schwarz comparison of the main mean-square terms
nonclaims: The theorem proves no asymptotic for fixed alpha>1.
The theorem is not the full sine-kernel interval pair-correlation law.
Exact nonnegativity is a later refinement relative to the theorem as printed.

name: Montgomery's test-function pairing and Fourier-support boundary
hypotheses: r and its displayed Fourier transform are integrable enough for Fourier inversion and exchange with the finite pair sum
primary_support_boundary: Because the printed theorem is uniform only on compact subintervals of (-1,1), the paper mainly restricts to hat_r_M vanishing outside [-1+delta,1-delta]. Goldston's later endpoint refinement permits support through [-1,1].
convention_map: Goldston uses the opposite Fourier sign; hat_r_G(alpha)=hat_r_M(-alpha). Since F_M is even, the two displayed pairings agree after alpha reflection. See MORPH-20260824-0010.
nonclaims: Knowledge of the transform only on |alpha|<1 does not determine arbitrary interval indicators or the full pair measure.
The support restriction is an information boundary, not a normalization choice.

name: Montgomery's Poisson-kernel explicit formula with all retained terms
hypotheses: RH in the paper's real-gamma notation
the initial Landau identity excludes x=1 and prime powers; continuity restores all x>=1 after subtraction
functional_equation_refinement: Using (zeta'/zeta)(1-sigma+i*t)=-(zeta'/zeta)(sigma-i*t)-log(tau)+O_sigma(1) and the absolutely convergent Dirichlet series in Re(sigma)>1 gives the two prime sums plus x^(1/2-sigma+i*t)(log tau+O_sigma(1))+O_sigma(x^(1/2)*tau^(-2))+O_sigma(x^(-2)*tau^(-1)).
term_types: two prime-sum ranges n<=x and n>x
specialization: At sigma=3/2, multiplication by x^(1/2-i*t) gives the algebraically equivalent a_n(x) presentation in Goldston's equation (3.11), with a_n(x)=min((n/x)^(1/2),(x/n)^(3/2)).
nonclaims: No term is discarded or merged in the recorded full identity.
The interface to a general Guinand-Weil formula remains MORPH-20260824-0005, not an asserted identity.

name: Mean-square proof route and the alpha=1 barrier
proof_route: set sigma=3/2 in LITSTMT-20260824-0028 and call the two sides L(x,t)=R(x,t)
after controlling ordinates outside [0,T] and evaluating the Cauchy-kernel convolution by residues, set x=T^alpha to obtain integral_0^T |L(T^alpha,t)|^2 dt=F_M(alpha,T)*T*log T+O(log^3 T)
apply the quantitative mean-value identity integral_0^T|sum a_n*n^(-i*t)|^2dt=sum|a_n|^2(T+O(n))
use the prime number theorem with error term to obtain T(log x+O(1))+O(x log x) for the prime-sum mean square
compare the logarithmic term, transition range, and prime-sum term by Cauchy-Schwarz
range_obstruction: When alpha>1, x=T^alpha exceeds T; the O(x log x) term and a second remainder are no longer smaller than the main term, and off-diagonal sums of Lambda(n)Lambda(n+h) cannot be ignored.
nonclaims: The obstruction is an identified missing off-diagonal estimate, not evidence that the conjectural continuation is false.
Replacing the off-diagonal sums by Hardy-Littlewood expectations is heuristic input, recorded separately in LITSTMT-20260824-0031.

name: Montgomery's signed-interval pair-correlation conjecture
statement: sum over 0<gamma,gamma'<=T with 2*pi*a/log(T)<=gamma-gamma'<=2*pi*b/log(T) of 1 is asymptotic to [integral_a^b (1-(sin(pi*u)/(pi*u))^2)du + delta(a,b)]*(T/(2*pi))*log T, where delta(a,b)=1 if 0 belongs to [a,b] and 0 otherwise.
diagonal_data: The delta term is the contribution of gamma=gamma' when the signed interval contains zero.
relation_to_F_conjecture: The paper heuristically proposes F_M(alpha,T)=1+o(1) for alpha>=1 uniformly in bounded intervals and calls that assertion and the signed-interval law essentially equivalent; this is not presented as a formal biconditional proof. Goldston later separates SPC from PCC and proves a one-way implication under stated hypotheses.
positive_interval_specialization: For 0<a<b, swapping the ordered pair (gamma,gamma') gives an exact bijection between the paper's positive signed-difference count and the opposite orientation used in Goldston's PCC. At an interval containing zero, diagonal multiplicity must be retained or explicitly subtracted.
nonclaims: The full sine-kernel law is not LITSTMT-20260824-0026.
The conjecture supplies no pointwise map from individual zeros to matrix eigenvalues.

name: Prime-pair and q-analogue evidence beyond alpha=1
heuristic_steps: expand the mean square beyond x>T and collect off-diagonal terms into sums of the form sum_{n<=y}Lambda(n)Lambda(n+h)
replace these sums by conjectural main terms c(h)y
assume a reasonable bound for the errors sum_{n<=y}Lambda(n)Lambda(n+h)-c(h)y to continue the program for 1<=alpha<2
add independence across h to motivate the same order for all alpha>=1
compare with a character-averaged q-analogue whose established ranges show no expected phase change
conclusion_motivated: F_M(alpha,T)=1+o(1) for alpha>=1 uniformly in bounded intervals.
nonclaims: Neither the Hardy-Littlewood substitution nor independence of the h-errors is proved in the paper.
The q-analogue is evidence by analogy, not a morphism from its character average to the zeta-zero pair form.

name: Primary correction of the theorem/conjecture collapse in the physics survey
corrections_and_sharpenings: the 1973 theorem proves the formula only for fixed 0<=alpha<1, uniformly through 1-epsilon, and states only eventual lower bound -epsilon for all alpha
the source separately labels the signed-interval sine-kernel law CONJECTURE
the paper's remark that the F-conjecture and interval law are essentially equivalent is informal; Goldston's later SPC/PCC distinction must be preserved
the primary source itself records the random-complex-Hermitian/unitary comparison as motivation after the conjecture, not as a proof of the conjecture
later_refinements_kept_separate: Goldston's squared-integral presentation gives exact nonnegativity
a later sieve refinement reaches alpha=1
Goldston's PCC orientation excludes the diagonal and is a specialization/re-expression, not the literal printed signed-interval formula
nonclaim: This record corrects the survey's attribution without claiming that every later formulation is textually identical to Montgomery's 1973 notation.

name: Dyson comparison, determinant k-correlation proposal, and operator nonclaim
source_claims: Dyson pointed out that the large-order random complex Hermitian or unitary pair correlation is 1-(sin(pi*u)/(pi*u))^2
the real-symmetric and symplectic form factors are different and nonlinear for 0<alpha<1
the proposed k-tuple correlation is det[A], with A_ii=1 and A_ij=sin(pi*(u_i-u_j))/(pi*(u_i-u_j)) for i not equal to j
the analogy motivates liminf(gamma_{n+1}-gamma_n)log gamma_n=0 and limsup(gamma_{n+1}-gamma_n)log gamma_n=+infinity
operator_language: The paper says the conjecture fits the view that an undiscovered linear operator may characterize the zeros and suggests complex Hermitian or unitary symmetry if such an operator exists.
nonclaims: No operator is constructed.
No map from zeros to eigenvalues is supplied.
The cited Mehta finite/large-matrix results have not yet been independently content-read as a primary RMT tranche.
Pair-correlation agreement does not identify finite GUE and CUE ensembles.

name: Simple-zero proportion and normalized-gap consequences
hypothesis: RH
consequences: the kernel calculation gives at least (2/3-o(1))*N(T) simple zeros
the proof produces a constant lambda<1 with liminf_n (gamma_{n+1}-gamma_n)log(gamma_n)/(2*pi)<=lambda; the paper explicitly says its calculation permits lambda=0.68
a complementary argument yields limsup_n (gamma_{n+1}-gamma_n)log(gamma_n)/(2*pi)>=lambda' for some lambda'>1
later_numerical_refinement: Goldston's later exposition reports Montgomery's bound as 0.669...; that later sharpening is not substituted for the 0.68 value explicitly printed in the 1973 proof.
nonclaims: The corollaries do not prove all zeros simple.
They do not prove the conjectural zero and infinite extreme-gap limits recorded later in the paper.

name: Guinand half-line test coordinate, cosine transform, zero ordering, and global hypothesis
hypothesis: The truth of the Riemann hypothesis is assumed throughout the paper.
coordinates: nontrivial zeros are written 1/2+i*gamma and multiplicities multiply their summands
an integral carrying limits -infinity and +infinity denotes the balanced limit lim_{X->infinity} integral_{-X}^X
prime_convention: p ranges over primes, m over positive integers, and a dash on a cutoff sum halves a term lying exactly at the endpoint.
nonclaims: No unconditional theorem is stated in this paper.
The half-line cosine presentation is not a general Hecke/idèle presentation.

name: Guinand order-3/2 Hankel pair and exact zero-count inversion
hypothesis: Riemann hypothesis

objects.G(x): the explicit expression in equation 2.9 containing the half-weighted prime-power cutoff, 4*sinh(x/2), log((x/4)coth(x/4)), arctan(exp(-x/2)), and pi/4

claims: G is the Hankel transform of order 3/2 of F
the Lp inversion and Parseval lemmas retain 1<p<=2 and p'=p/(p-1)
bounded variation gives the averaged point value [F(y+0)+F(y-0)]/2
Theorem 2 gives the exact averaged value [N(T+0)+N(T-0)]/2 through a limit of Lambda sums, sine kernels, arg Gamma(1/4+iT/2), and retained elementary terms
nonclaims: Theorem 2 does not erase the average at a jump.
The Hankel presentation has not been identified with Weil's local-place distribution merely from the shared subject.

name: Guinand Theorem 3 with boundary term and balanced zero density
hypotheses: f is an integral, tends to zero at infinity, and x*f'(x) belongs to L^p(0,infinity) for some 1<p<=2

definitions.P_f(T): dash-sum over 0<m log p<T of (log p)*p^(-m/2)*f(m log p)

boundary_removal: Theorem 3-prime permits omission of f(T)[P_1(T)-2e^(T/2)] if either the prime error estimate sum_{n<=N}Lambda(n)-N=O(N^(1/2)log^alpha N) holds with alpha=1/p, or T^(1/2)f(T)->0.
nonclaims: The boundary term is part of Theorem 3 and is not silently discarded.
The displayed theorem is RH-conditional and does not become unconditional by a change of variables.

name: Guinand additive-log to multiplicative-prime coordinate
fibres_and_exceptional_loci: exp:R->R_{>0} and log are two-sided inverses with singleton fibres; the endpoints T and U remain related and are not forgotten.
nonclaim: The coordinate change alone does not identify the archimedean or zero distributions with Weil's formula.

name: Guinand power test and reciprocal prime/zero resonances
claims: for f(x)=x^(-s), initially 1/2<Re(s)<1, the cosine transform is sqrt(2/pi)*Gamma(1-s)sin(pi*s/2)*x^(s-1), and the archimedean integral is analytically continued with retained eta and zeta terms
the compact cosine cutoff f(x)=cos(yx)-cos(yX) for 0<=x<=X and zero for x>=X gives a -X+O(1) term exactly when y equals a positive zero ordinate gamma, and O(1) otherwise
inversely, sum_{0<gamma<X}cos(y*gamma)=-(X/(2*pi))*(log p)/p^(m/2)+O(log X) when y=m log p, and O(log X) otherwise
hypothesis: Riemann hypothesis
nonclaims: The resonance statements do not construct an operator.
Theorem 5 is explicitly noted to follow from a known theorem cited by Guinand.

name: Weil Hecke L-function, completed function, and contour control
objects: number field k of degree d
idèle group I_k, principal idèles P_k, and class group C_k=I_k/P_k
character chi of C_k with conductor f and archimedean data eta_lambda, f_lambda, phi_lambda
the associated-character representative satisfying sum_lambda eta_lambda*phi_lambda=0
equations: A=(2*pi)^(-d)|Delta|Nf and Lambda(s)=G(s)L(s) with G carrying the displayed gamma factors
analytic_control: poles at 0 and 1 occur for the trivial character and are absent otherwise
zeros are counted with multiplicity and their number in T<=|Im(s)|<=T+1 is O(log T)
selected horizontal contours avoid zeros and satisfy |Lambda'/Lambda(s)|<=B(log|m|)^2 in the retained strip
nonclaim: This setup is more general than Guinand's zeta-specific RH-conditional setting; generality does not by itself prove a termwise specialization.

name: Weil logarithmic Mellin test space and PF regularization
transform: Phi(s)=integral_{-infinity}^{infinity}F(x)e^((s-1/2)x)dx; Weil's footnote identifies this as the conventional Mellin transform of v^(-1/2)F(log v).
condition_A: F is continuous and continuously differentiable except at finitely many points a_i; F and F' have first-kind jumps there, and F(a_i)=[F(a_i+0)+F(a_i-0)]/2.
condition_B: There exists b>0 such that F(x) and F'(x) are O(e^(-(1/2+b)|x|)).

name: Genus-one product for the Riemann zeta function
statement: DLMF gives zeta(s) as the exact displayed elementary prefactor times product over zeros rho with Re(rho)>0 of (1-s/rho) exp(s/rho).
use_boundary: The manuscript retains every prefactor and uses McMullen's factorization theorem for the choice-free centered regrouping. It does not infer an ordering-free packet product merely from the typography of DLMF's product.

name: Reciprocal-gamma product
statement: 1/Gamma(z)=z exp(gamma z) product_(k>=1)(1+z/k) exp(-z/k).
use_boundary: The manuscript substitutes z=s/2 literally, keeps the Euler-constant exponential and every elementary factor, and proves the O(n^-2) normal-convergence bound for logarithmic differentiation.

name: Zeta value and first derivative at zero
statement: zeta(0)=-1/2 and zeta'(0)=-(1/2) log(2pi).
use_boundary: These constants crosswalk the local source's zero-end expansion. Their use does not absorb or renormalize the completed-function prefactors.

name: Negative-even zeta zeros and derivative values
hypothesis: n is a positive integer; equation 25.6.13 gives the stated derivative family for positive derivative order k.
statement: zeta(-2n)=0. In the k=1 specialization of the derivative-value formula, zeta'(-2n)=(-1)^n (2n)! zeta(2n+1)/(2(2pi)^(2n)), which is nonzero.
use_boundary: The nonzero first derivative proves simplicity of each negative-even zero at this proof site. This is a positive cited result, not an inference from a missing proof elsewhere.

name: Laurent expansion of zeta at its simple pole
statement: zeta(s)=1/(s-1)+sum_(n>=0)(-1)^n gamma_n (s-1)^n/n!, with the Stieltjes constants gamma_n.
use_boundary: The local analytic-completion source's expansion is crosswalked to this identity; subsequent completed-function and packet formulas retain their separate factors and proofs.

name: Scale-invariant Riemann-sum transform and its common zeros
hypothesis: f is an even Schwartz function on R with integral zero; z lies in Im(z)>-1/2 for the continued factorization and in |Im(z)|<1/2 for the common-zero statement.
statement: The multiplicative Fourier transform of E(f)(u)=u^(1/2) sum_(n>=1) f(nu) equals zeta(1/2-iz) psi_f(z). In the open strip, the zeros of zeta(1/2-iz) are the common zeros of this transform family. The explicit f0(x)=exp(-pi x^2)(2pi x^2-1) has psi_f0(z)=(1/4)pi^(-1/4+iz/2)(-1-2iz)Gamma(1/4-iz/2).
proof_coordinates: Fubini first gives the factorization for Im(z)>1/2
the zero-integral condition and the Poisson estimate continue both sides to Im(z)>-1/2
the explicit multiplier is nonzero in the open strip
use_boundary: Chapter 18 proves the stronger multiplicity-level common-divisor equality in the open strip. It explicitly does not extend the equality globally, where transformed trivial zeros occur.

name: Spectrum of Delta=H(1+H) on the strong-Schwartz trace quotient
statement: On strong(R_+^*) modulo the closure of range(tr composed with Delta), the spectrum of Delta is the set, counted with possible multiplicities, of (rho-1/2)^2-1/4 over nonreal zeta zeros rho.
proof_coordinates: Mellin transform identifies the function spaces with Schwartz spaces on vertical strips
the quotient decomposes into finite-dimensional projection ranges
evaluation at a zero rho uses a jet space of dimension n_rho
multiplication by -s(1-s) has a triangular matrix with n_rho identical diagonal entries -rho(1-rho)
use_boundary: Chapter 18 proves the exact affine formula -z^2-1/4, the sign fibres, conjugation orbit, packet polynomial, and divisor pushforward. The cited source is not attributed those independent coordinate refinements.

name: Scaling Site H0 quotient and the critical-zero Schwartz quotient
statement: The induced R_+^* action on H^0(Scaling Site,L^2/closure(Sigma E)) is canonically isomorphic to the action by multiplication with r^(is) on S(R) modulo the closure of the ideal generated by zeta(1/2+is).
proof_coordinates: the plus/minus one Fourier components identify global L2 sections with a pair of smooth rapidly vanishing functions
the global-section quotient map is proved surjective
the substitution s=plus/minus 2pi/L identifies the two closed ideals
a multiple critical zero may supply a nilpotent Jordan term of order bounded by its multiplicity
use_boundary: Chapter 18 proves only the exact shared coordinate chain from a critical packet through its Laplacian value to frequency and circle length. It records a Boolean-to-Scaling-Site sheaf morphism as an unconstructed obligation at this proof site, not as a nonexistence claim.

name: Theorem 6.4(ii): fixed critical ordinate and every positive-integer cycle length
hypothesis: s>0 and zeta(1/2+is)=0.
statement: For each n in Z_{>=1}, the circle C_mu of length L=2pi n/s is a zeta-cycle. The proof constructs the character chi(u)=u^(is) on C_mu=R_+^*/mu^Z and places it in the orthogonal complement of Sigma_mu E(S_0).
proof_coordinates: mu=exp(L)
mu^(is)=exp(i s L)=exp(2pi i n)=1, hence chi descends
the Mellin identity has factor zeta(1/2+is), so chi is orthogonal to every Sigma_mu E(f)
finite covers preserve the zeta-cycle condition
source_text_discrepancy: The theorem statement's final subspace phrase conflicts with its own proof; the proof, the immediately following H(L)=Sigma_mu E(S_0)^perp, and the 2023 restatement use the orthogonal complement.
use_boundary: For this fixed s, n=1 gives the least member of the displayed positive-integer family. No statement compares it with lengths attached to other ordinates or calls it globally primitive.

name: Exact Fourier-index to Schwartz-coordinate sign in the Scaling Site realization
statement: For L>0, Fourier index k uses kernel u^(-2pi i k/L), its R_+^* action is r^(-2pi i k/L), and comparison with the Schwartz action r^(is) gives the exact coordinate s_k(L)=-2pi k/L.
proof_coordinates: the pointwise Fourier transform defines index k with exponent -2pi i k/L
the generated ideal contains zeta(1/2-2pi i k/L)
the scaling action multiplies the k component by r^(-2pi i k/L)
therefore at L=2pi n/nu the labeled pair is (+n,-nu,r^(-i nu)) and (-n,+nu,r^(+i nu))
use_boundary: The two signs and their labels are retained. This coordinate comparison does not choose a nonzero quotient vector, global section, or sheaf morphism from the Boolean packet sheaf.

name: Two-place p-infinity semilocal quotient, generic unit fibre, and p-boundary circle
hypotheses: p is a rational prime and U={+-p^n:n in Z} acts diagonally on Q_p x R.
statement: The semilocal quotient X_(p,infinity)=(Q_p x R)/U carries the invariant |x|_p|y|. Every nonzero fibre is Z_p^*, the x=0,y!=0 boundary is R_+^*/p^Z, and its logarithmic scale is R/(log p)Z.
proof_coordinates: fundamental domain Z_p^* x R_+^* on the generic stratum
T_p is x=0,y!=0 modulo U
the map g is the class of |y| in R_+^*/p^Z
the source explicitly asks how the totally disconnected generic fibre ties to the torus in the zero limit
use_boundary: The audit constructs the complete orbit topology and local quotient map from these coordinates. The source is not attributed the later six-term boundary computation or Morita obstruction.

name: Free proper transformation-group imprimitivity and six-term K-theory functoriality
hypotheses: X is locally compact Hausdorff, G is locally compact, and the action is free and proper.
statement: The integrated covariant representation identifies C_0(X) crossed product G with K(L(X)), hence strongly Morita equivalent to C_0(X/G); C*-extensions induce the periodic six-term exact sequence, and K-theory is Morita invariant.
proof_coordinates: L(X) is the completion of C_c(X) with the quotient-valued inner product
C_0(X) and G act covariantly
the crossed product maps isomorphically to compact module operators
Bott periodicity closes the six-term sequence
use_boundary: Applied separately to the complete local and semilocal free proper actions. Compatibility for the particular open-boundary extension is proved from the restricted modules in the manuscript rather than silently assumed.

name: Explicit K_0-to-K_1 exponential boundary map
hypotheses: 0 to J to A to A/J to 0 is an exact sequence and e is a quotient idempotent with lift x in a matrix algebra over A^+.
statement: The connecting map sends [e]-[p_n] to [exp(2 pi i x)] in K_1(J).
proof_coordinates: Theorem 9.3.1 gives the six-term exact sequence
Section 9.3.2 names this arrow the exponential map and prints the lift formula
use_boundary: With the explicit continuous lift phi(t)=1/(1+e^t), the manuscript computes the winding and retains the declared generator sign rather than normalizing it away.

name: Primitive-spectrum invariance under strong Morita equivalence
statement: The canonical ideal-space bijection induced by an imprimitivity bimodule is a homeomorphism because it is a lattice isomorphism; on primitive ideals the recorded topology is the hull-kernel topology.
proof_coordinates: the ideal topology is defined by the displayed subbasis
the topology restricts to the ordinary primitive-ideal hull-kernel topology
the imprimitivity correspondence is a lattice isomorphism and hence a homeomorphism
use_boundary: The manuscript combines this invariant with an explicit local-connectedness obstruction between the two commutative orbit spaces. It does not infer non-equivalence from different presentations.

name: Finite-dimensional spectral-flow convention
hypotheses: A continuous path of finite-dimensional self-adjoint matrices; the endpoint-signature formula is integer-valued when both endpoints are invertible.
statement: Spectral flow counts negative-to-positive crossings positively and equals one half of the final signature minus the initial signature.
use_boundary: For F_t=(1-2t)I_2, Sf(F)=-2 and Sf(-F)=+2. Both signs are retained; no orientation normalization is made.

name: Finite-dimensional whole-line spectral flow as Fredholm index
hypotheses: H_t is a continuous path of self-adjoint N by N matrices on R with invertible limits H_{-infinity} and H_{+infinity}; D_H=d/dt-H_t has domain W^{1,2}(R,C^N) and codomain L^2(R,C^N).
statement: D_H is Fredholm and Ind(D_H)=-Sf(H). The proof concludes Ind(D_H)=dim E^u(H_{-infinity})-dim E^u(H_{+infinity}).
proof_coordinates: coercive estimate modulo compact interval
Rellich compactness gives closed range and finite kernel
kernel and cokernel are expressed by stable and unstable subspaces
endpoint dimension calculation yields the signature and spectral-flow formula
use_boundary: For D=d/dt+F=d/dt-(-F), the exact whole-line index is -Sf(-F)=-2. This theorem does not assign an index to an unspecified compact-interval APS realization.

name: Full and reduced crossed products and amenability criterion
statement: The full crossed product is the completion in the supremum over covariant representations; the reduced crossed product is the completion in the regular Hilbert-module representation; the canonical full-to-reduced map is an isomorphism for amenable groups.
use_boundary: Together with the explicit invariant mean on Z/2 and the manuscript's orbit matrices, this justifies completing the coordinate algebra in the regular supremum norm without conflating full and reduced presentations.

name: Amenable-group Fell bundles have faithful regular representation
hypotheses: B is a Fell bundle over an amenable group G.
statement: B has the approximation property; the regular representation Lambda:C*(B)->C*_red(B) is injective, hence the full and reduced cross-sectional algebras coincide.
proof_coordinates: an amenability net and an approximate identity produce a Cesaro net
the Cesaro maps factor through the reduced algebra
pointwise convergence to the identity forces Ker Lambda=0
use_boundary: For the semidirect-product Fell bundle of C_0(R) under the reflection action of Z/2, the displayed invariant mean proves the group amenable, so the explicit regular orbit-matrix norm is the full crossed-product norm.

corrected_statement: Mesland--Şengün Sections 1.3.16-1.3.20 define covariant representations, the full crossed-product norm, the regular Hilbert-module representation, the reduced norm, and the full-to-reduced quotient. On the content-read pages they state the amenability equivalence only for the group-algebra map C*(G)->C*_r(G), not the action-level full-to-reduced theorem used here.
replacement_dependency: LITSTMT-20260829-0149 supplies the required Fell-bundle theorem for an arbitrary semidirect-product bundle over the amenable group Z/2.
use_boundary: Retain LITSTMT-20260829-0148 only for the norm definitions and regular representation; do not use its original last clause as source evidence.

name: Brown-Green-Rieffel stable isomorphism theorem
hypotheses: B and E are C*-algebras with countable approximate identities (equivalently here, separable algebras with strictly positive elements).
statement: B and E are strongly Morita equivalent if and only if B tensor K and E tensor K are isomorphic.
proof_coordinates: an imprimitivity bimodule produces a linking algebra with B and E as complementary full corners
strictly positive elements in the two corners give one in the linking algebra
the full-corner stabilization theorem makes each corner stably isomorphic to the linking algebra
use_boundary: Applied only to each proved finite-prime ideal I_p strongly Morita equivalent to C_0(R), yielding an existence isomorphism I_p tensor K -> C_0(R) tensor K. The manuscript records and explicitly corrects its induced orientation sign.

name: Busby reconstruction and addition over a stable ideal
hypotheses: 0 -> B -> E -> A -> 0 is a C*-extension; for the additive construction B is stable.
statement: An extension is recovered as the pullback of M(B)->Q(B) along its Busby invariant. For stable B, orthogonal matrix corners followed by a standard stable isomorphism define addition of extension classes.
use_boundary: The manuscript writes the finite orthogonal-corner formula directly in M(C_0(R) tensor K), checks it is a star-homomorphism, and forms the pullback rather than invoking an unidentified K-group map.

name: Covariant push-forward of stable extensions in the ideal
hypotheses: sigma:B_1->B_2 is a star-homomorphism, B_1 is sigma-unital, and extensions are stabilized.
statement: The induced multiplier/corona map pushes an extension of A by B_1 to an extension of A by B_2, and this push-forward is additive.
use_boundary: The concrete map mu_P has an explicitly written multiplier extension and corona quotient, so the global Busby invariant is the exact push-forward of the direct-sum local invariant.

name: Naturality of six-term connecting maps
hypotheses: A commutative morphism of short exact C*-algebra sequences.
statement: K-theory is a stable completely additive homology theory, and its connecting homomorphisms are natural for morphisms of short exact sequences.
use_boundary: For the explicit extension diagram with quotient identity and ideal map mu_P, the bottom boundary equals (mu_P)_* composed with the direct-sum local boundary, fixing the sign and every retained coordinate.

name: Mapping-torus kernel-cokernel computation
hypotheses: A is a C*-algebra and alpha is a star-automorphism; M_alpha consists of continuous paths f on [0,1] with f(1)=alpha(f(0)).
statement: The mapping torus fits into 0 -> SA -> M_alpha -> A -> 0, and, after the Bott identification, both connecting maps are 1-alpha_*. Equivalently its K-groups are controlled by the kernels and cokernels of 1-alpha_* in the associated cyclic six-term sequence.
proof_coordinates: evaluation at zero is the quotient map
the kernel is the suspension SA
a projection p is lifted by t p +(1-t) alpha(p)
the exponential boundary is the Bott image of [p]-[alpha(p)]
the other connecting map follows by suspension
use_boundary: Applied to A=C(Y_{p,P}) and the explicit translation automorphism sigma_p. The source does not compute the resulting profinite invariant/coinvariant groups or any semilocal boundary map; those are independently proved coordinate by coordinate in the live manuscript.

name: Induction in stages is internal tensor-product composition
hypotheses: H subset K subset G are closed groupoids, the displayed groupoid correspondences induce C*(K)-C*(H) and C*(G)-C*(K) correspondences, and pi is a representation of C*(H).
statement: The composite correspondence is the internal tensor product, and induction through K agrees with direct induction from H to G.
use_boundary: The finite-set coherence manuscript independently writes the semilocal transition homeomorphism, crossed-product matrix units, and triple-inclusion equality. This source is cited for the standard correspondence-level interpretation of that exact staged composition, not as a replacement for the coordinate proof.
nonclaim: No theorem in the source is used to infer that arbitrary independently chosen stabilization isomorphisms are coherent.
